record.original_question: What particle-physics model, field, or mechanism caused early-universe inflation, what is the inflaton if a new scalar field drove the exponential expansion, and what caused inflation to stop rather than continue until the present?

evidence.quote: There are serious indications that, at an early stage of its evolution, the Universe experienced a period of intense exponential expansion, called inflation (see e.g. [78, 103].
It may be related to the presence of a new, absent in SM, scalar field, the inflaton.
For a particle physicist, at least two questions arise: first, what is the nature of the inflaton, and second, what was the reason for the inflation to stop and not to continue until now.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Cosmological observations indicate that the very early Universe underwent a phase of nearly exponential (de Sitter–like) accelerated expansion, called inflation, which is not accounted for by the matter content of the Standard Model of particle physics. A common theoretical framework attributes this expansion to a scalar field φ (the "inflaton"), minimally coupled to gravity, with action

   S = ∫ d^4x √(−g) [ M_P^2 R / 2 − (1/2) g^{μν} ∂_μ φ ∂_ν φ − V(φ) ],

where M_P is the reduced Planck mass and V(φ) is a scalar potential. In a spatially flat Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker background with Hubble rate H, the homogeneous inflaton obeys φ̈ + 3H φ̇ + V'(φ) = 0 and 3M_P^2 H^2 = (1/2) φ̇^2 + V(φ); slow-roll inflation occurs when ε := (M_P^2/2)(V'/V)^2 ≪ 1 and |η| := M_P^2 |V''/V| ≪ 1, and ends when these conditions are violated.

Identify, within particle physics:

(a) a concrete model, field content, or microscopic mechanism that drives such an inflationary epoch in the early Universe;

(b) the precise nature of the inflaton — i.e. if a new scalar field beyond the Standard Model is responsible for the exponential expansion, specify what this field is, how it couples to known matter, and what determines the form of V(φ);

(c) the dynamical mechanism that terminates inflation (e.g. the breakdown of slow roll and subsequent reheating) rather than allowing the de Sitter-like phase to persist to the present epoch, together with the conditions under which this termination occurs and the Universe transitions to a hot radiation-dominated phase consistent with observed cosmology.
artifact.status_search_result: The identity of the inflaton and the precise particle-physics mechanism for inflation and its termination remain open as of 2026. Many candidate models exist (Higgs inflation, Starobinsky R+R^2, axion/natural inflation, hybrid inflation, supergravity- and string-motivated scenarios), and CMB data (Planck, BICEP/Keck) continue to constrain but not single out a model. No consensus identification of the inflaton has been established.

status_evidence.title: Planck 2018 results. X. Constraints on inflation
status_evidence.snippet: Planck data constrain but do not uniquely determine the inflationary model; many single-field slow-roll models remain compatible.
status_evidence.claim: The microscopic identity of the inflaton is not fixed by current data.

status_evidence.title: BICEP/Keck 2021 constraints on primordial gravitational waves
status_evidence.snippet: Upper limits on the tensor-to-scalar ratio rule out some inflationary potentials but leave a broad class viable.
status_evidence.claim: Inflationary model-building remains an active open problem.

status_evidence.title: Encyclopaedia Inflationaris (updated)
status_evidence.snippet: A comprehensive catalog of inflationary models continues to be maintained, reflecting that the inflaton has not been identified.
status_evidence.claim: The nature of the inflaton is still unknown.
